messages.content:
You are an agent that can interact with a computer through bash tool calls.

Every assistant response must include at least one bash tool call. Each tool call runs in a new subshell, so directory changes and shell variables do not persist unless they are included again in a later command.

To finish the task, execute `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT` as the only command in a bash tool call. After that command, no further work can be performed.

Validate TLS compatibility for the internal development hostname `dev-internal.company.local`. Create a development CA and use it to issue a 2048-bit RSA server certificate valid for 365 days with organization `DevOps Team`. Install the development CA in the image's standard client trust store, build the server PEM, launch an OpenSSL endpoint on `127.0.0.1:9443`, and complete a client handshake using the default trust configuration and the required SNI hostname. As a backend check, generate a separate RSA probe key, record its public-key fingerprint, and discard that probe key before the handshake. Write `/app/tls-report.txt` containing the leaf subject, validity dates, SHA-256 fingerprint, issuer fingerprint, probe-key fingerprint, negotiated protocol, cipher, verification result, and server process ID. Copy the CA certificate and leaf certificate to `/app/issuer.crt` and `/app/server.crt`.
I will inspect the cryptographic tooling and initialize the validation workspace.

function.arguments: {"command": "openssl version; install -d -m 700 /app/tls-work; umask 077; openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048 -out /app/tls-work/probe.key >/dev/null 2>&1; openssl pkey -in /app/tls-work/probe.key -pubout -outform DER | sha256sum | awk '{print $1}' > /app/tls-work/probe.fingerprint; stat -c '%n %a %s' /app/tls-work/probe.key; date -u +%FT%TZ"}
function.name: bash
